Static RAG is dead, Agents are next.

Most people think RAG is advanced AI.

It’s not.

It’s just the starting point.

This visual shows the real shift happening right now:

RAG vs Agentic RAG

Here’s the difference in simple terms:

🔹 RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)

– Fetches relevant documents
– Feeds them to the LLM
– Generates an answer

➡️ Linear. One-shot. Limited thinking.

🔹 Agentic RAG

– Rewrites your query
– Decides what info is missing
– Chooses the best data source (DB, APIs, web)
– Iterates until the answer is actually good

➡️ Dynamic. Iterative. Goal-driven.

The big insight?

RAG retrieves information.

Agentic RAG thinks about how to retrieve better information.

If you're building AI products, this shift isn’t optional it’s inevitable.

Save this if you’re working on AI systems.

Entry-level Android hiring dropped 25% in 2025-26.

At the lowest levels — some companies cut over 70%.

I know that sounds scary. But here is the full picture:

Senior Android engineers: still in high demand.
KMP developers: 25% YoY growth in job postings.
Developers who can architect and debug: irreplaceable.

The market is not collapsing for Android devs.
It is collapsing for developers who stopped growing after learning the framework.

What separates the ones thriving right now:

→ They understand what happens below the API
→ They can review AI output and know when it is wrong
→ They think in systems, not screens

The path from junior to irreplaceable in 2026:

Stop building features.
Start understanding why things work.

If you are early in your career — this is not a reason to quit.
It is a reason to go deeper, faster.

What skill are you going deep on? 👇
